versions: Xyce 7.10, IHP SG13G2 Xyce model libraries

entries.gap: Xyce rejects the PSP 103 model cards of the PDK: no LV or HV MOS device simulates.
entries.symptom: Unrecognized parameter D for device YPSP103_VA!M1 (sg13g2_moslv_mod.lib, sg13g2_moshv_mod.lib)
entries.workaround: Simulate decks with MOS devices in ngspice. Use Xyce only for decks without MOS devices (for example HBT harmonic balance). Do not replace the PSP cards with another MOS model.

entries.gap: Xyce rejects the r3_cmc card of the poly resistors rsil, rppd and rhigh.
entries.workaround: In Xyce, replace each poly resistor by an ideal resistor with the value that ngspice gives for the same corner and temperature, and state the substitution; the voltage coefficient is then lost. Otherwise simulate in ngspice.

entries.gap: The Xyce library of the PDK does not define the HV varactor subcircuit sg13_hv_svaricap.
entries.symptom: Subcircuit SG13_HV_SVARICAP has not been defined
entries.workaround: Simulate varactor circuits (VCO tanks) in ngspice. For Xyce harmonic balance, use a capacitor fitted to the ngspice C(V) at the bias point, and state it.

entries.gap: The npn13G2 card computes the transit time tf from the global temperature. A per-instance dtemp at a global 27 C leaves tf at its 27 C value.
entries.symptom: With the global temperature at -40 C or 125 C, the HB of an HBT circuit often fails (DC point failed, or no HB Newton convergence) where 27 C converges. A per-instance dtemp alone gives no message but a wrong tf: at 125 C the device is too fast (optimistic), at -40 C too slow; tf scales with ((T + 273) / 300)^0.7.
entries.workaround: Use temperature_method dtemp_tf of the xyce hb operation (also hb_limits): a global 27 C, dtemp = T - 27 on every npn13G2 instance, and vbic_tf of a copy of the corner section scaled by ((T + 273) / 300)^0.7. The MIM capacitors and other devices stay at 27 C.
entries.evidence: PDK file sg13g2_hbt_mod.lib (tf expression); found in a detector block of a reference design; a PA output stage task: global temperature fails at -40 C and 125 C (typ and corners), dtemp_tf converges at all four tested cases

entries.gap: In harmonic balance at 122 GHz, the lead currents of npn13G2 (IC, IB of the Q element) include the charging currents of the junction capacitances. Their instantaneous minimum and maximum are not the conduction currents. Xyce HB gives no internal junction voltages of the VBIC model.
entries.symptom: The terminal base current of a large-signal PA stage swings by tens of mA (minimum -42 mA in a 122 GHz cascode driver), so a reversal of the instantaneous base current (avalanche) or a peak current per emitter cannot be read from it.
entries.workaround: Check the cycle means (exact: a charging current has zero mean over a period) and the peak terminal voltages (operation hb_limits, gate limits on an hb experiment). The instantaneous conduction current needs a DC table of the device at the internal junction voltages (as in the ngspice oscillator operation); for HB it is not run.
entries.evidence: simulated, Xyce 7.10, IHP SG13G2: the terminal base current of the cascode driver of a public 122 GHz radar PA (minimum -42 mA, cycle mean +14 to +37 uA); the hb_limits container run of a 61 GHz CE stage

entries.gap: With the excess phase on in both simulators (ngspice sw_nqs=1), the ngspice and the Xyce HBT cards of the PDK agree at 27 C and do not have the same temperature dependence of the small-signal parameters.
entries.symptom: No message. One npn13G2 at equal collector current: y21 of Xyce against ngspice is +0.7 to +1.2 % at -40 C, -0.3 to -0.5 % at 27 C and -2.6 to -4.2 % at 125 C (phase +2 degrees at -40 C, -4 degrees at 125 C), with the same sign at the typical, slow and fast HBT corners. At equal base voltage the difference is larger: Nx 4 at VBE 0.88 V, VCE 1.2 V, 125 C: DC current 1.9 %, y21 5.2 % at 61 GHz and 8.9 % at 122.5 GHz, y11 7.5 % at 122.5 GHz (Xyce lower).
entries.workaround: None in the models. Run the device check at the corner temperatures of the design: operation device_crosscheck with temp_c and reference_temp_c, or the device_check gate with the corner conditions; it reports a difference at a corner temperature as a temperature finding when the 27 C values agree. Treat a hot or cold row that both simulators contribute to (for example ngspice stability and Xyce harmonic balance) as uncertain by this difference, and state it. Which simulator is closer to silicon is not known.
entries.evidence: simulated, ngspice 46 and Xyce 7.10, IHP SG13G2: the design record of a public 122 GHz radar design (equal collector current; -40, 27 and 125 C; typical, slow and fast HBT); device_crosscheck in the environment image at 125 C with reference 27 C (test device-crosscheck-container): 0 findings at 27 C, 7 temperature findings at 125 C; the device_check gate of the task evals/pa-stage-sg13g2 (Nx 8, slow and fast HBT, -40 and 125 C, equal base voltage): y21 at 122.5 GHz 3.3 to 4.3 % apart at -40 C and 9.1 to 10.5 % at 125 C. Not run: the cause in the model equations (which temperature coefficient differs)
